summary: The Worker Client Refresh example in the SDK documentation is confusing as it only shows a simple connection string scenario, which doesn't demonstrate the actual use case requiring client refresh (custom authentication). This leads users to misunderstand how to properly implement it.
userImpact: Users attempting to implement custom authentication with Worker Client Refresh are confused by examples that don't show this use case, leading to incorrect implementations and runtime errors.
rootCause: The example documentation only demonstrates simple connection string scenarios and doesn't show real-world custom authentication use cases where client refresh is actually needed.
proposedFix: Update the Worker Client Refresh example to show a custom authentication scenario with periodic client updates, similar to the implementation provided by the issue author with background service and authentication token handling.
workaround: The issue author provided a complete example implementation using a background service (TemporalAuthUpdaterService) to periodically check and update the client with new authentication credentials.
resolutionDetails: The example documentation was improved with a more realistic custom authentication scenario; a file watcher-based refresh example was added in #617.
keyQuote: The example uses a connection string for connecting to Temporal which sort of removes the need for refreshing the client.
